summary.headline: DCB Bank Q4 FY26 record PAT of INR 206 crore (FY26 INR 732 crore), NIM up 12bps QoQ to 3.39%, GNPA 2.45%, NNPA 0.89%.
summary.overview: DCB Bank reported its third consecutive record quarterly profit, with Q4 PAT at INR 206 crore and FY26 PAT at INR 732 crore, with income growth of 16% against expense growth of 11%. Advances grew 18% YoY and 6% QoQ, deposits grew 21% YoY and 7% QoQ, and cost of deposits fell 44bps YoY. Asset quality improved, with slippage ratio down to 2.28% from 3.09%, FY26 credit cost at 40bps, and recoveries and upgrades at 109% of fresh slippage. Management flagged the West Asia conflict as a cloud on the horizon but said no immediate portfolio impact is visible yet.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever quarterly PAT; third successive record quarter
Highest ever; fee growth 9% QoQ per analyst question
Q1 was 59bps; guidance was no more than 45bps
Q4 at 2.47% (other statements say 2.4%); includes INR 27 crore wage code charge in Q3
Absolute decline QoQ; target was below 15%

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Co-lending gold book about INR 8,366 crore plus own gold book about INR 4,000 crore; gold is about 21% of advances with slippage of 5.3% versus 1.4% for the rest of the book. Gold slippage was 6.29% a year ago.

segments.name: Mortgages
segments.commentary: Mortgage book grew about 3.8% QoQ (about 6.5% in the first nine months, 10% for FY26 per analyst); management says new self-sourced BL/HL mix is improving growth each quarter. MFI book reduced from about INR 1,400 crore to INR 600-700 crore.

segments.name: SME / MSME
segments.commentary: SME book about INR 2,000 crore, flat QoQ and down about 13% YoY; TReDS about INR 300 crore. New vertical for tickets above INR 3 crore launched from July.

segments.name: Agri and others
segments.commentary: Growth from tractors, KCC, construction finance, educational and institutional loans, and corporate. Management says the non-co-lending book grew about 8.6% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: Deposit repricing tailwind expected to last until late Q2 or early Q3 FY27, then stop.
Credit cost to remain below 45bps; through-the-cycle model 45-55bps; current levels 32-33bps per management.
Cost to average assets expected to stay around 2.5%, with headcount rising to about 13,000 from current levels.
Co-lending growth in FY27 to be in line with overall asset growth; co-lending share to decline further.
Asset growth of 18-20% described as a given; management cautious given West Asia conflict.
Net NPA to remain below 1%. A fundraise of about INR 1,100-1,200 crore (INR 1,500 crore enabling resolution) planned for late Q2 or early Q3 FY27.
Branches expected to cross 500 during FY27; NIM business-model target 3.50-3.65% with CASA and cost of deposit as levers.
capex_capacity: Branch network: 11 branches added in Q4; management says branches are optional and more than 500 expected during the year.
Headcount expected to rise to about 13,000 from current levels (Sept 2024 level was 9,100), with additions aimed at liability and deposit acquisition and distribution.
Liquidity deliberately over-stocked as a buffer given West Asia uncertainty.
Capital: board enabling resolution for INR 1,500 crore; intended raise about INR 1,100-1,200 crore (around USD 100 million).
demand_pricing: Growth focus on secured, small-ticket and granular products: mortgage, corporate, gold loans, agri, tractors, KCC, construction finance and education loans.
Mortgage mix shifting toward self-sourced over DSA; management says DSA dependence must come down.
Current account growth flat while SA grew 10%; management calls this the key gap. Retail term deposit rate gap versus large banks narrowed to about 0.60-0.61% from 1.27%.
Bulk deposits about 20% of deposits; bank now manages granularity, rate and tenor together.
Treasury fees nil in Q4; growth driven by third-party distribution, forex and trade income.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit repricing benefit to NIM continue, and is HL to BL sourcing still 60-40?
qa_highlights.answer: Repricing benefit expected until late Q2 or early Q3; HL to BL sourcing is now about 70-30, helping yield and credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM rise 12bps QoQ when yield on advances was flat and cost of funds fell only slightly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no one-offs; the benefit came from a mix shift as lower-yield co-lending shrank while higher-yield book grew, absorbing the 25bps repo cut; better recoveries also helped.

qa_highlights.question: Gold slippage versus overall slippage numbers did not reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Vishal Anchaliya said gold has 21% weightage with 5.3% slippage and other products 79% with 1.4%, giving 2.28% overall.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth be sustained with co-lending moderating and MSME flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Co-lending growth to match overall asset growth in FY27 (it grew 24.9% in FY26 versus 108% earlier); non-co-lending growth was 8.6% QoQ; mortgages reengineered and growing.

qa_highlights.question: What drives NIM towards the 3.50-3.65% business-model target?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposit management, current account growth and not chasing high-yield segments; execution risk rather than strategic risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fundraise plan and provision coverage level?
qa_highlights.answer: Raise about INR 1,100-1,200 crore around late Q2 or early Q3 FY27 at current prices; management said PCR above 75% is acceptable, 78%+ good.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and hydrocarbon price pass-through could hit lower-income borrowers; duration of the conflict is the key unknown.
Gold loan slippage at 5.3% and co-lending transition to the new CLM framework; management says the transition is complete for gold but not across all products.
Bulk deposits at about 20% of deposits and flat CA growth could limit further cost-of-deposit benefit after Q2 FY27.
Yield on advances down 56bps YoY; NIM expansion depends on cost of deposits as the repricing benefit fades.
SME book stagnant; recovery depends on the new above-INR 3 crore vertical.
Q4 seasonality in slippage and recoveries is only partly explained (April appraisal cycle); worth checking in Q1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, asset quality and deposit cost, but cautious on growth and the West Asia macro risk. Management was candid about gaps (flat current account, slow cross-sell, mortgage slowdown) and sometimes deflected precise numeric questions.
key_quotes: The profit after tax for Q4 is at INR 206 crores and the full year is at INR 732 crores, both of which are the highest ever in the history of the bank.
There are clouds in the horizon on account of West Asia crisis. We are being cautious.
So as of now, we're sticking to the below 45 bps, okay?
I don't see our net NPA going back above 1%.

adds.what: 11 branches added in Q4 FY26; more than 500 branches expected during FY27
Headcount rise to about 13,000 by end of FY27 (from 9,100 in Sept 2024), aimed at liability and deposit acquisition

growth.why: Management calls 18-20% balance sheet growth a given over 3-4 years, backed by 11 branches added in Q4 with 500+ branches targeted in FY27 and headcount rising to ~13,000, plus a deposit repricing tailwind to late Q2/early Q3 FY27; no order book or hard capacity numbers beyond branches, and management itself is cautious on West Asia.
